summary: Build telecom regulatory compliance and consumer protection skills with practical templates, QoS tools, and regulator-ready reporting. Enrol now.
lede: Telecom compliance applies licensing obligations, service-quality requirements, competition rules, and consumer-protection processes to daily operations. For professionals in regulatory affairs, compliance, consumer care, or service quality, the course supports building obligation matrices and licensing checklists, handling complaints, monitoring QoS indicators, and reviewing tariffs and market conduct. It also covers risk-based gap assessment, automated compliance tracking, and performance reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is built for you if you work where telecom regulation meets day-to-day operations, customer protection, and executive reporting. It fits professionals who already handle licensing, QoS monitoring, complaints, or legal reviews and need a more structured way to prove compliance and protect customers. Telecom Regulatory Compliance Officers who track licence conditions and obligations. Regulatory Affairs Specialists who manage filings, consultations, and regulator correspondence. Consumer Protection Managers who oversee complaint resolution and service transparency. Quality of Service Analysts who measure outages, availability, and KPI trends. Licensing and Permits Officers who maintain renewal calendars and control evidence. Telecom Legal Counsel who review obligations, disputes, and enforcement exposure. Interconnection and Access Managers who monitor access terms and conduct risk. Network Governance Leads who align operational controls with compliance requirements. Customer Experience Managers who manage billing disputes and service recovery. Compliance Reporting Analysts who prepare dashboards for leadership and regulators.
prerequisites: You should bring familiarity with telecom operations, regulatory correspondence, customer complaint logs, or service-performance reporting. A laptop is recommended for workshop exercises, and sample internal documents such as a licence schedule, complaint register, or QoS report will make the applied work more relevant.
